title: RBAC v2 / Audit -> SIEM Field Mapping and Connector Validation Spec
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, developer-friendly spec for translating Redwood RBAC v2 and platform audit events into schemas suitable for customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, Azure Sentinel). The doc combines mapping rules, redaction/PII guidance, evidence-automation triggers, ingestion validation checks, and on-boarding checklist items for connector engineers and customer SREs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Input: RBAC v2 audit events produced by Redwood Private/Dedicated/Hosted control planes and the service runtime audit stream.
- Targets: Splunk HEC, Datadog Log Intake, Azure Sentinel (Common Event Format / Azure Monitor).
- We assume events are emitted as newline-delimited JSON over HTTPS or forwarded via a customer syslog/collector.
- Goal: preserve security-relevant attributes (actor, action, resource, decision, request_id, timestamp, outcome) while meeting common SIEM field expectations.

High-level mapping principles:
1) Single canonical audit schema internally, then transform per-target. Keep canonical names stable: event_time, event_id, principal.type, principal.id, principal.role, action, resource.type, resource.id, decision, reason, client_ip, user_agent, request_path, request_params (redacted), prev_state (diffs), outcome.severity, correlation_id.
2) Explicit redaction: PII/credentials must be removed or hashed before leaving the control plane. Use placeholder values for sensitive fields (e.g., "<REDACTED:email>").
3) Preserve original payload as base64-encoded compressed blob when customers request full-evidence, gated by contract. Store as evidence_blob in the canonical schema.
4) Map severity/decision semantics to SIEM-native fields (e.g., Splunk -> severity, Datadog -> status, Sentinel -> AlertSeverity).

Canonical -> Splunk HEC mapping (recommended):
- event_time -> _time (epoch ms / ISO8601 in ext_time)
- event_id -> event_id
- correlation_id -> correlation_id
- principal.type -> principal_type
- principal.id -> principal_id
- principal.role -> principal_role
- action -> action (e.g., "deploy_model", "grant_role", "token_issue")
- resource.type -> resource_type
- resource.id -> resource_id
- decision -> decision (ALLOW/DENY)
- reason -> decision_reason
- client_ip -> src_ip
- user_agent -> user_agent
- request_path -> http_path
- request_params -> http_params_redacted
- outcome.severity -> severity (map: info=1, low=2, medium=4, high=6, critical=8)
- evidence_blob -> evidence_blob (base64; if permitted)

Canonical -> Datadog mapping notes:
- Datadog uses attributes: @timestamp, host, service, ddsource, ddtags. We push: @timestamp = event_time, service = "redwood-audit", ddsource = "redwood-rbac-v2", ddtags = "env:prod,tenant:<tenant_id>". Key fields should be repeated as top-level attributes for facets: principal_id, principal_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, decision, correlation_id.
- Map severity to Datadog status tag: status:info|warning|error|critical.

Canonical -> Azure Sentinel / CEF mapping:
- Use Common Event Format (CEF) with extension fields. Map event_time -> DeviceCustomDate or TimeGenerated. Use fields: src=client_ip deviceCustomString1=principal_id, deviceEventClassId=action, request=create(resource_id), cs1Label=correlation_id.
- When using Azure Monitor logs ingestion, place canonical JSON into the "AuditLogs_CL" custom log table for KQL queries.

Field-level transformation rules and examples:
- principal.id: prefer immutable identifiers (user_id/service_account_id). If only email exists, hash with HMAC-SHA256(customer-salt) and include truncated prefix for support (first 8 chars).
- request_params: remove values for keys in SENSITIVE_PARAM_SET = ["authorization", "password", "token", "ssn", "email"]. Keep the structure and key names; set values to "<REDACTED>".
- prev_state: include only keys relevant to the decision (e.g., role grants) and limit size to 16KB. If larger, set prev_state_summary with a small diff and point to evidence_blob if contract allows.

Evidence automation integration (how SIEM triggers map back to Redwood evidence):
- Use consistent correlation_id across runtime logs, audit events, and evidence snapshots. SIEM saved searches should surface correlation_id for automated evidence export requests.
- Recommended saved-search triggers: (1) any DENY on privileged action; (2) role_change for tenant_admins; (3) API key creation outside of ScheduledWindow. On trigger, automation should call Redwood evidence API with correlation_id -> returns evidence_bundle (signed, timebound).
- For customers with evidence-automation enabled: the connector must support an endpoint for evidence retrieval callbacks (webhook) and include signed URL or a short-lived token embedded in the SIEM alert.

Connector operational requirements (bandwidth, batching, retry):
- Target throughput: connectors should support bursts up to 1k EPS for enterprise tenants, sustained 200 EPS.
- Batch size: prefer 50-200 events per HTTP request for Splunk HEC/Datadog. Use gzip compression.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with cap 60s, max 5 retries. On 413 PayloadTooLarge return, fall back to splitting events.
- Ordering: no strict ordering guarantee required for SIEM ingestion, but each event must include event_time. For forensic flows where ordering matters, provide sequence_number field and enable sequence reassembly on the SIEM side.

Validation and onboarding checklist (developer / customer SRE):
- [ ] Confirm contract/per-tenant evidence permissions and whether evidence_blob allowed to be shipped.
- [ ] Validate timezone handling: all event_time in ISO8601 UTC.
- [ ] Test redaction: send sample event with email and token and ensure downstream values are "<REDACTED:email>", "<REDACTED:token>".
- [ ] Confirm mapping of severity levels and a sample alert in customer SIEM maps to intended priority.
- [ ] Verify correlation_id is present in runtime logs (app logs) and audit events.
- [ ] Run sample saved-search triggers that request evidence and confirm evidence webhook flow completes within SLA.
- [ ] Confirm fields required by customer detection use-cases (e.g., principal_role, tenant_id) are present as searchable facets.

Customer requirements matrix (examples):
- Customer A (regulated-finance): requires evidence_blob disabled, HSM-signed event headers, 7-year retention guidance -> implement packaged export with signed digest and long-term storage patterns.
- Customer B (SaaS-platform): accepts full evidence, prefers Datadog, requires role-change alerts routed to PagerDuty -> configure connector to apply datadog tags and include correlation_id.

Field redaction policy (short):
- Always redact values for keys matching sensitive patterns (emails, keys, tokens, cc numbers).
- Hash identifiers that must be de-identified but still linkable within customer's environment using HMAC with customer salt.
- Add a metadata flag redaction_policy_version in each exported event.

Sample payloads (illustrative):
- Splunk HEC (event body JSON):
  {"event_time":"2025-03-11T22:14:20Z","event_id":"evt-9132","principal_id":"usr-7f2b6a","principal_role":"platform-admin","action":"grant_role","resource_type":"project","resource_id":"proj-42","decision":"ALLOW","decision_reason":"policy:ok","client_ip":"18.205.33.4","correlation_id":"corr-0a9"} 

- Datadog example attributes: @timestamp=2025-03-11T22:14:20Z, service=redwood-audit, ddsource=redwood-rbac-v2, principal_id=usr-7f2b6a, action=grant_role, decision=ALLOW, correlation_id=corr-0a9

Telemetry and observability for the connector itself:
- Emit connector_health events with status {uptime, last_success, queue_depth, last_http_status}. Ship connector metrics to customer metrics endpoint or Redwood console.
- Add debug mode for onboarding that redacts tokens but preserves full structure. Debug mode should be time-limited and require explicit opt-in.

Security controls and auth patterns for connectors:
- Use mutual TLS or API keys scoped to tenant and export type. Rotate keys quarterly.
- For Splunk HEC, recommend HEC Token + TLS + source IP allowlist.
- For Datadog, use ingest API keys with tag restrictions and post-ingest filtering.

Edge cases and special notes:
- If an audit event is >128KB after canonicalization, truncate non-critical fields and attach a 64KB evidence summary. Flag event with oversized=true.
- When customers operate in air-gapped environments, produce signed archived export bundles (tgz) that map one-to-one with the canonical schema and include a manifest.json (manifest must be plain object but in the export bundle; internal logs will keep canonical JSON).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Standardize numeric severity mapping across all SIEM targets (proposal: map RBAC severity to CEF/LEEF integer scale).
- Q2: Should we include raw request headers in evidence_blob by default for enterprise tenants? Need legal/PRIV review.
- TODO: implement a lightweight schema registry entry for canonical audit schema and publish avro/jsonschema (JIRA-SEC-521).

Next steps for delivery:
1) Lock canonical audit schema in Confluence and publish schema versions.
2) Implement exporter library support for Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel with redaction hooks and tests.
3) Trial with three pilot customers (one per vertical) and iterate mapping.

References:
- RBAC v2 design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design
- Evidence API: https://internal-api.redwood.ai/docs/evidence
- Connector repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-exporter

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is written as a working onboarding playbook rather than a signed-spec. Expect follow-ups to tighten numeric mappings and add schema artifacts.
- If you're testing, use the sample payloads above and flag any missing fields required by your detection rules.
notes: work-in-progress; some fields intentionally terse for iteration
